domain_assessment.domain: Underground mining operations, specifically drill-and-blast planning for a sublevel open stope
domain_assessment.objective: Execute a production blast on schedule while achieving usable fragmentation for mill feed and remaining within peak particle velocity limits near a service shaft.
domain_assessment.incident_type: A blast round involving a newly mapped fault trace, localized wet blast holes, sensor disagreement over vibration readings, and an inconclusive post-blast overbreak/fragmentation outcome.

decision_points.summary: The engineer chooses a limited geotechnical spot-check near a newly mapped fault trace rather than either conducting a full resurvey or proceeding with no additional verification.
evidence_before: Geology mapped a minor fault trace crossing approximately one third of the panel.
Moisture was observed along the trace.
The mine was already a shift behind and the mill was low on feed.
A full geotechnical resurvey would consume the available shift.
evidence_after: The spot-check was clean for the three tested holes.
The engineer explicitly recognized that the spot-check did not cover the full fault-affected stretch.
Additional wet holes were later identified near and outside the checked area.
The fault-zone section later showed overbreak and coarser fragmentation.
goals_constraints: Maintain blast schedule and restore mill feed.
Obtain current information about the fault zone.
Avoid an operationally costly full-shift delay.
Preserve blast safety and acceptable blast performance.
alternatives: Perform a limited spot-check near the fault trace.
decision_points.decision_basis: A constrained, intermediate verification strategy: obtain some current, case-specific evidence while acknowledging that full verification was not feasible within the schedule.
decision_points.time_pressure: Material but not portrayed as eliminating deliberation: the round was already behind schedule and a full resurvey would have consumed the shift.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate to high. The fault was newly mapped, moisture was present, and the limited check could not establish conditions throughout the affected zone.

decision_points.summary: The engineer adopts mixed charging: emulsion decking for specifically flagged wet holes and ANFO for the rest of the panel.
evidence_before: The spot-check did not cover the entire fault-affected zone.
Several holes near the trace logged wet after drilling.
The explosives technician flagged specific wet holes and proposed emulsion decking.
The engineer had prior experience with wet ground producing variable behavior.
evidence_after: One additional borderline-wet hole was discovered during loading outside the original flagged list.
The charging plan had already been largely set when that later condition was detected.
The fault-zone section later exhibited overbreak and coarser fragmentation.
goals_constraints: Adjust charging where current evidence indicated water-related risk.
Avoid applying a broader treatment without a specific technical basis.
Maintain practical loading progress and schedule.
Manage uncertain blast performance in variable ground.
alternatives: Use emulsion/decking for the entire panel.
Apply emulsion/decking only to technician-flagged holes and retain ANFO elsewhere.
decision_points.decision_basis: Joint consideration of technician observations, the localized character of the wet-hole evidence, and bounded prior experience that wet ground can behave differently across cases.
decision_points.time_pressure: Present through the broader production schedule, but no text indicates that the decision was rushed or that available evidence was ignored because of time.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate. The known wet conditions were localized, but incomplete coverage meant additional wet holes could exist outside the original flagged set.

decision_points.summary: The engineer selects a more conservative longer-interval timing sequence after two vibration sensors near the shaft provide discrepant readings.
evidence_before: The round was adjacent to a service shaft, making vibration control operationally important.
One sensor indicated a comfortably compliant vibration level while the other was borderline.
Vendor guidance did not specify which sensor should govern for this particular geometry.
The engineer consulted the safety officer.
evidence_after: Both sensors remained under the vibration limit after firing.
The margin was smaller than usual.
The engineer accepted some potential fragmentation-efficiency cost to increase the safety margin.
goals_constraints: Remain below PPV limits near the service shaft.
Resolve an instrumentation conflict without clear vendor guidance.
Avoid defaulting to the standard sequence without reviewing the discrepancy.
alternatives: Treat the lower-risk sensor reading as controlling.
Treat the more conservative borderline reading as controlling and use a longer interval.
decision_points.decision_basis: Precautionary weighting of the more safety-constraining reading after consultation, because neither sensor could be shown to be wrong and the disagreement remained unexplained.
decision_points.time_pressure: Limited. The engineer reports that there was some pressure to proceed but sufficient time for a ten-minute consultation with the safety officer.
decision_points.uncertainty: High with respect to which sensor better represented the actual vibration risk for the geometry; low regarding the appropriateness of discussing and conservatively managing that unresolved uncertainty.

decision_points.summary: Following overbreak and coarse fragmentation in the fault-zone section, the engineer declines to attribute the outcome to a single cause and requests additional geological/instrumentation review before changing the next round.
evidence_before: The fault-zone section displayed overbreak and coarser fragmentation.
The prior spot-check left parts of the fault-affected area unobserved.
The charging approach was mixed rather than uniform.
The engineer recognized a visually similar overbreak pattern from a previous site.
evidence_after: The engineer tells the mine manager that both incomplete geological coverage and mixed charging are plausible contributors.
The engineer requests review of current instrumentation before altering the next round.
The engineer declines to provide a falsely definitive explanation despite pressure for an actionable account.
goals_constraints: Provide an operationally useful explanation to the mine manager.
Avoid falsely attributing a multifactor outcome to one cause.
Identify information that could support a safer and more effective adjustment for the next blast.
Respond credibly despite management pressure for a clean explanation.
alternatives: Attribute overbreak primarily to the fault trace.
Attribute overbreak primarily to the mixed charging design.
State that multiple plausible causes remain unresolved and obtain further review before changing the next round.
decision_points.decision_basis: Explicit multi-cause reasoning, recognition of incomplete evidence, and refusal to elevate a familiar past pattern into a conclusive causal attribution.
decision_points.time_pressure: Low to moderate. There was managerial pressure for an immediately actionable explanation, but no evidence that the engineer was required to make an irreversible immediate decision.
decision_points.uncertainty: High. The available evidence does not discriminate adequately between fault-related conditions, incomplete wet-hole detection, charging variation, or their interaction.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I went with that for the flagged holes only, keeping ANFO for the rest of the panel — partly on his data, partly because I'd handled similar wet ground before without major issues.” Later, the participant adds: “I've seen wet ground behave both ways — sometimes it's nothing, sometimes it needs real adjustment — so I wasn't relying purely on his numbers or purely on my own read.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Charging-decision account and follow-up probe concerning the mixed charging approach.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No supported experience-bias mechanism is present. Prior experience is referenced, but it is explicitly bounded by acknowledgment of variable wet-ground behavior and is combined with current technician data. The participant does not substitute familiar prior cases for present evidence, dismiss contrary evidence on experiential grounds, or treat past success as determinative.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Appropriate expert integration of prior operational knowledge with case-specific observations, accompanied by explicit recognition that prior cases are not uniform analogues.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: To support experience bias, the text would need evidence that the engineer discounted, overrode, or failed to seek case-specific technical evidence because a familiar prior wet-ground episode was treated as sufficient proof. Such evidence is intentionally absent and should remain absent in this zero-occurrence control.

revision.location: Decision point 2, charging-decision answer and follow-up answer.
revision.current_defect: None for the control requirement. The experiential reference is adequately counterbalanced within the same reasoning episode.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the current explicit statement that wet ground can behave differently and that the decision relied on both technician data and operational experience.
preserve: The participant's qualified reference to prior wet-ground experience.
The explicit acknowledgment that experience alone cannot resolve the case.
avoid_creating: Any wording that makes prior successful wet-ground cases the decisive reason for retaining ANFO.
Any dismissal of newly observed moisture or technician evidence on the basis of familiarity.
Any post-blast assertion that prior experience proves the cause of overbreak.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “A full geotechnical resurvey would've eaten the whole shift, which we didn't have, so I had the crew run a limited spot-check on a handful of holes near the trace instead — a middle option between doing nothing and doing everything.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Initial situation account and later pattern-decision probe.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No supported status quo-bias mechanism is present. Although the existing pattern history contributes to the engineer's provisional confidence, the engineer does not simply retain the normal approach. The response includes a genuine verification action, records the coverage limitation, and treats the check as an intermediate response to newly observed conditions.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A proportionate risk-management decision under a real operational constraint: limited inspection is selected because full inspection is costly and no inspection is inadequate.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: To support status quo bias, the text would need evidence that the engineer retained the standard pattern principally because it was familiar or customary despite the fault information, without meaningful verification or reconsideration. The current text directly negates that mechanism.

revision.location: Decision point 1, initial situation account and pattern-decision follow-up.
revision.current_defect: None for the control requirement. The text makes the verification step distinct from passive retention of the prior approach.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the explicit contrast among doing nothing, conducting a full resurvey, and performing a limited spot-check, along with the participant's acknowledgment of incomplete coverage.
preserve: The schedule pressure and mill-feed constraint.
The fault trace and moisture premise.
The limited spot-check as a real data-gathering action.
The stated limitation that the checked holes did not represent the entire fault-affected stretch.
avoid_creating: Language such as “we always use this pattern” as the primary decision rationale.
A statement that the fault trace was ignored because previous rounds had worked.
Removal of the spot-check or removal of the stated coverage limitation.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “The technician's data pointed pretty specifically at certain holes, and I didn't have a strong reason to extend that to the whole panel.” The participant also states: “I've seen wet ground behave both ways” and “I wasn't relying purely on his numbers or purely on my own read.”
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No supported overconfidence mechanism is present. The engineer expresses neither unwarranted certainty in the charging plan nor confidence that the available observations fully characterize the panel. The account recognizes localized evidence, variable ground behavior, and later discovery of an unanticipated borderline-wet hole.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Calibrated operational judgment using incomplete localized evidence, with subsequent acknowledgment that the initial evidence set did not cover all potentially relevant holes.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: To support overconfidence bias, the text would need a clearly excessive certainty claim, unjustified belief that the initial flagged-hole set was complete, or an unexamined override of technician data. The interview instead shows uncertainty calibration and joint reliance on evidence sources.

revision.location: Decision point 2, mixed-charging explanation; reinforced in the post-blast diagnostic discussion.
revision.current_defect: None for the control requirement. The account explicitly acknowledges the limits of both evidence and experience.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the statements that the technician data were specific to certain holes, that wet ground can behave differently, and that the later borderline-wet hole had not been detected when the plan was set.
preserve: The distinction between known flagged holes and subsequently discovered conditions.
The participant's acknowledgment that the plan was set under incomplete coverage.
The later refusal to claim a single certain explanation for overbreak.
avoid_creating: Absolute statements that the flagged-hole list captured all wet holes.
Claims that the engineer knew the rest of the panel was dry without full coverage.
A retrospective claim that the mixed plan was certainly correct or certainly caused the observed outcome.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “A full geotechnical resurvey would've eaten the whole shift, which we didn't have, so I had the crew run a limited spot-check ... a middle option between doing nothing and doing everything.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A potentially acceptable-but-incomplete information-gathering action is selected under schedule constraints rather than maximizing verification coverage.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The text supplies a proportionate and transparent risk-management rationale, not evidence of premature closure or an unexamined “good enough” threshold. The participant actively identifies the residual information gap.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “It looked similar to a fault-zone overbreak pattern I'd seen at a previous site, but this round also had real gaps ... Either factor could explain what we saw, maybe both together.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A familiar prior pattern could have served as an initial causal anchor for interpreting the overbreak.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant immediately qualifies the analogy, identifies competing explanations, declines to select one story, and requests additional review. There is no evidence that the familiar pattern distorted subsequent evidence weighting.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Either factor could explain what we saw, maybe both together. I told the manager that rather than picking one story.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A post-outcome assessment could have judged the earlier decisions solely from the undesirable overbreak and fragmentation result.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant reconstructs the information available at the time, distinguishes the later-discovered wet hole from the original charging-plan evidence, and avoids treating the unfavorable outcome as proof that a particular earlier decision was wrong.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “We agreed the conservative reading deserved more weight given we couldn't fully explain the gap between the two.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The engineer gives greater weight to the reading associated with higher vibration risk.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is justified safety-sensitive decision-making under unresolved measurement disagreement near a service shaft. The participant consults the safety officer and accepts a known performance trade-off rather than acting from unsupported fear.

nonbias_cues.location: Decision point 2, initial charging account and charging-decision follow-up.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Prior experience is not treated as conclusive. It is explicitly counterbalanced by technician data and recognition that wet ground has behaved differently across previous cases.

nonbias_cues.cue: Reliance on the pattern's history in the ground
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The pattern history supplies provisional confidence but does not produce passive retention of the existing approach. The engineer orders a current spot-check and identifies its limited coverage as a known residual risk.

nonbias_cues.cue: Limited spot-check instead of a full resurvey
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: An incomplete check can reflect constrained optimization, not bias. The participant identifies the alternatives, explains the operational constraint, gathers additional evidence, and remains aware that the evidence is incomplete.

nonbias_cues.cue: Selection of the more conservative sensor interpretation
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: In a shaft-adjacent blast with unresolved instrument disagreement, conservatively managing a safety limit after consulting a safety officer is defensible risk management rather than evidence of a cognitive distortion.

nonbias_cues.cue: Overbreak and coarse fragmentation after the blast
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: An unfavorable outcome does not establish that an earlier decision was biased. The text does not retrospectively equate outcome quality with decision quality.

nonbias_cues.cue: Inability to identify one cause of the overbreak immediately
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The uncertainty arises from genuinely incomplete and potentially interacting evidence. The participant does not make an unsupported causal claim, and explicitly seeks additional review.

Time pressure and stakeholder pressure can influence decisions, but neither alone demonstrates a specific bias mechanism. Here, the interview documents deliberation, consultation, and disclosure of uncertainty.

causal_claims.claim: The fault trace, incomplete geotechnical coverage, wet-hole conditions, mixed charging, or an interaction among these factors may have contributed to overbreak and coarse fragmentation.
causal_claims.assessment: The participant identifies multiple plausible causal pathways but does not claim that the available evidence can discriminate among them.

causal_claims.claim: A full geotechnical coverage check might have detected additional wet holes earlier and could have enabled broader charging adjustment.
causal_claims.assessment: This is a plausible process counterfactual. The participant appropriately avoids claiming that earlier detection would certainly have changed the overbreak outcome.

causal_claims.claim: Using longer timing intervals was expected to provide a wider vibration margin than the less conservative sequence.
causal_claims.assessment: The claim is consistent with the decision rationale and is supported by post-blast readings remaining under the limit, although the text does not establish a comparative causal estimate because the alternative sequence was not observed.

causal_claims.claim: Agreement between the two sensors would have made the timing decision simpler.
causal_claims.assessment: The statement concerns reduced ambiguity in decision-making, not a claim that sensor agreement would have changed blast performance.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The visual resemblance between the observed overbreak and a fault-zone pattern from a previous site could be mistaken for causal proof.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The participant immediately identifies incomplete coverage and mixed charging as alternative explanations, declines to select a single cause, and seeks a geological/instrumentation review.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The coexistence of overbreak with mixed charging could be overread as proof that the charging choice caused the result.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The participant notes that the charging design was only one of several unresolved explanatory factors and does not infer causation from temporal or spatial association alone.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Post-blast vibration compliance could be overread as proof that the chosen longer timing sequence was uniquely necessary or optimal.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation_in_text: The interview reports the observed compliant result but does not claim that an alternative timing sequence would necessarily have exceeded limits.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Extent of geotechnical spot-check coverage, hypothetically changed from partial coverage to coverage of the entire fault-affected zone.
held_constant: The broad operational context and schedule pressure.
The observed possibility of wet holes near the trace.
The causal question of whether earlier information would have altered charging and/or overbreak.
causal_audit.explanation: The interview contains a limited but well-formed counterfactual probe. It isolates expanded geotechnical coverage and traces a plausible informational pathway: broader coverage could identify additional wet holes earlier, which could permit a broader charging adjustment. Crucially, the participant does not add a second causal change or claim certainty that the outcome would have differed. The sensor-agreement hypothetical is also coherent but concerns decision uncertainty rather than the causal production of the blast outcome.

global_revision_constraints: Maintain the zero-occurrence control condition for Experience Bias, Status quo bias, and Overconfidence Bias.
Do not reinterpret ordinary operational constraints, expert experience, safety conservatism, or unfavorable blast outcomes as bias without a specific evidence-processing mechanism.
Preserve the explicit qualifications that distinguish prior experience from experience bias, a limited verification action from status quo bias, and calibrated uncertainty from overconfidence.
Preserve the multi-cause post-blast diagnosis and the participant's refusal to claim causal certainty from incomplete evidence.
